critical_code_review_comments: OK · P0 durable slot link (scalp/engine.py L1620-1648): The `await db.trades.update_one({...}, {'$set': {'submission_slot': dict(slot)}})` is properly awaited and its matched_count is the gate. On matched_count != 1 (or exception): trade is marked `submission_state='uncertain_slot_link'`, the decision is stamped `dataset='submitted_uncertain'` + `reject_stage='slot_link_failed'` + `order_submit_ts_ms`, and the function RETURNS at L1648 — strictly BEFORE the `self._emit(db, 'BrokerSubmitted', ...)` at L1649, the `broker_stats.record(submissions=1)` at L1652, and the two `record_open()` calls at L1654-1655. This is the safety property mandated by the review: BrokerSubmitted / open-risk accounting cannot fire on an unlinked/uncertain submission. The unlinked slot remains leased so sweep_submission_slots can reconcile.

OK · P1 fail-closed history policy (scalp/exec_quality.py + engine.py L1272): `broker_fill_count=(_prior.get('totals') or {}).get('fills') or 0` — when totals.fills < MIN_BROKER_FILLS_FOR_LIVE (20) the execution_quality() score is capped at INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY_MAX_SCORE (39), which is below EXEC_QUALITY_MIN (40) → live submission blocked regardless of otherwise-perfect conditions. Test `test_perfect_conditions_still_capped_without_fills` confirms score<=39, history_capped=True, score<gate_min even with spread_pctl=0, quote_age=100ms, slippage=0.05p, ack=500ms, vol_ratio=1.0.

OK · P1 broker priors in hot path (scalp/engine.py L1255-1272): Persisted per-(broker, session) priors survive restarts via `_prior = await broker_stats.summary(db, self.broker)`. Session is selected from UTC hour via `session_name(datetime.now(timezone.utc).hour)`. Both slippage and ack_latency inputs to execution_quality() are computed by `blend(local, prior, local_n)` — full trust in local at MIN_BROKER_FILLS_FOR_LIVE=20 samples, capped there (weight = min(local_n, 20)/20). Boundary tests confirm blend(0.2, 0.4, 0)=0.4, blend(0.2, 0.4, 10)=0.3, blend(0.2, 0.4, 20)=0.2, blend(0.2, 0.4, 50)=0.2.

OK · P1 thresholds versioning (scalp/exec_quality.py): THRESHOLDS_VERSION=1 stamped into every execution_quality() dict as `thresholds_version`. thresholds_snapshot() exposes {version:1, exec_quality_min:40, min_broker_fills_for_live:20, weights:{spread:22,...}}. GET /api/scalp/exec-calibration correctly returns this snapshot in the response so calibration analysis is anchored to a specific threshold set.

OK · Endpoint routing (routes/scalp_routes.py L43-89): GET /exec-calibration correctly buckets scalp_decisions on execution_quality.score into (0-39,40-59,60-79,80-100), aggregates n, live_submitted (dataset='submitted'), broker_rejected (dataset='attempt_failed'), history_capped, labeled outcomes, avg_net_pips, target_first_rate, reject_rate. All rows scoped to `user_id: user['id']` (per-user calibration; matches CQRS pattern in the rest of the app). GET /broker-stats returns per-session and totals aggregates with fills as expected.

OK · broker_stats.summary() (scalp/broker_stats.py L54-76): correctly exposes `fills` at BOTH per-session (`fills: int(doc.get('entry_slip_n') or 0)`) and totals level (`tot['fills'] += ...`) — this is the field the engine reads at engine.py L1272 to gate the fail-closed history cap.

OK · _stub_db fixture extension (tests/unit/scalp/test_scalp_unit.py L296-309): The stub now yields a synthetic scalp_broker_stats prior with 60 submissions / 1 reject / 40 fills across all 5 session buckets, so the new iter-61 fail-closed history cap doesn't accidentally block the stages under test in the 161 legacy scalp unit tests. All 161 pass with the extension.

OBSERVATION · exec-calibration's zero-filled buckets are semantically correct at this moment: execution_quality is only stamped on decisions reaching the pre-submit live path (engine.py L1276-1279 _bg update); no live-submitted decisions have been stamped yet in the preview DB, so all buckets legitimately report n=0. This is the expected 'no data yet' state, not a bug. Confirmed by problem-statement explicit note.

OBSERVATION · Endpoint auth uses get_current_user (any authenticated user), not admin_required — this is consistent with the rest of scalp_routes.py where per-user scoping is enforced downstream via user['id'] filters. Not a security concern. Unauth requests return 401/403 as verified.
